title: Palindrome Checker
story: 'racecar' spelled backwards is 'racecar'. 'A man a plan a canal Panama' — ignore spaces and case, and it reads the same both ways. Palindromes are wordplay's greatest hits. Build a checker that handles spaces, case, and punctuation.
why: Palindrome checking combines string manipulation, character comparison, and loop patterns — fundamental skills for any text processing task.
analogy: A mirror placed at the center of a palindrome should show the exact same word. 'racecar' — put a mirror after 'e' and you see 'rac' reflected as 'car'. Your two-pointer checker is two people reading from opposite ends, meeting in the middle, confirming every letter matches.
try_it: Add palindrome checking that ignores spaces and case. Test with "A man a plan a canal Panama" and "Never odd or even". Also handle single-character strings and empty strings. What about numbers? 12321 is a numeric palindrome.
tips: Two-pointer technique: left starts at 0, right at len-1, move toward center
Return false EARLY on first mismatch — no need to check the rest
Empty strings and single characters are technically palindromes
common_mistakes: Not adjusting right = s.len() - 1 — s.len() is one past the last index
Comparing left < right with <= — the center char doesn't need checking
Forgetting that string.get() returns Option — need .unwrap()
